newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sees first oil find by private firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sees first oil find by private firm.

text.p: Egypt's Ghareb Oil Fields started production at the first oil find by a private national firm, the company's chairman said on Thursday.
"We started production on Wednesday -- the first anniversary of our discovery," Saleh Mahmoud Awadallah told Reuters.

Two wells in the Western Desert field, called Burg al-Arab, produce 1,500 barrels per day (BPD), Awadallah said, adding that the figure would double in a year after the company drills two "After five years, we will be producing some 70,000 BPD," said Awadallah, who holds a 60 percent stake in the firm. "There is also great natural gas potentials in the concession."
Awadallah said the two wells were 3,600 metres (12,000 feet) deep and produce 41 API gravity crude at the depth of 2,300 metres. The oil stratum is about 20 metres thick.
Burg al-Arab is in al-Alamein concession. Other firms have their own oil and natural gas finds near the concession.
